thread:
maria: Hey team — I'm doing a small refactor to centralize provider pinning: moving the postgresql provider config out of modules/db-postgres into the root module and letting modules inherit it. Before I push, any immediate red flags? CI plan already failed locally for me with a lockfile mismatch.

jon: can you paste the exact error from terraform? usually that helps.

maria: Error snippet from CI: 
```
Error: Provider registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/postgresql: lock file mismatch

The dependency lock file .terraform.lock.hcl was created by a different provider version. Run \`terraform init -upgrade\` to update the lock file.
```

ishaan: ok — two quick things: 1) if you move provider config to root, make sure modules don't declare a different required_providers constraint (that can cause terraform to think it needs different plugins). 2) run `terraform init -upgrade` from the root and commit the updated .terraform.lock.hcl. CI will pick it up.

dana: also watch for aliased providers. if modules use `provider = postgresql.db` and you remove that alias, you may need `terraform state replace-provider` to map old resources to the new provider address.

jon: exact commands we've used before:
```bash
# regenerate lockfile for linux platform used in CI
terraform init -input=false -upgrade
terraform providers lock -platform=linux_amd64 -platform=darwin_arm64
```
That second command is handy if CI runs a specific platform.

maria: what about module version pins? db-postgres is coming from our private registry. Right now modules/db-postgres has no explicit version in root module since we use local path during development. Should I add a `version = "~> 2.0"` in the root module call to keep things stable?

ishaan: yes, put a conservative constraint (e.g. `~> 2.0`) in the module block in the root. And add a `required_providers` block in root with the pinned provider version:
```hcl
terraform {
  required_providers {
    postgresql = {
      source = "hashicorp/postgresql"
      version = "~> 1.5"
    }
  }
}
```
That prevents subtle drift between dev and CI.

dana: plus add a migration note in the module README showing a sample `terraform state replace-provider` command, e.g.:
```bash
terraform state replace-provider 'registry.terraform.io/-/postgresql' 'registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/postgresql'
```
so anyone who previously used a legacy provider address knows what to run.

infra-bot: CI: terragrunt-plan (eng-infra) failed — https://ci.company.net/builds/12345 (shows same lockfile error) :eyes:

maria: great notes. I'll: 1) add required_providers in root, 2) run `init -upgrade` and `providers lock` for CI platforms, 3) add module version pin in the root module call, 4) update module README with migration steps and `state replace-provider` example. I'll open a PR and tag @jon and @ishaan for quick review.

jon: looking forward to the PR, happy to review. :+1:

ishaan: ping me when the lockfile is in the branch, I'll run a local plan with the same platform flags.

maria: thanks all — opening PR in ~20m. :rocket:
